newsitem.title: UK: Watch out, now balloons are a health hazard.
newsitem.headline: Watch out, now balloons are a health hazard.

text.p: Christmas parties can be dangerous if balloons are involved, British doctors warned on Friday.
Blowing up balloons can damage the lungs, causing air bubbles to spread under the skin throughout the body.
Writing in the British Medical Journal, Dr Stuart Elborn and colleagues at Belfast City Hospital described the case of a 24-year-old man hospitalised for lung problems.
"He had inflated about 20 party balloons over one hour," they wrote. "He had not experienced chest pain or shortness of breath at the time or immediately afterwards," they added.
But 48 hours later the man was very ill. Air bubbles could be felt under the skin over his back and buttocks and there was a "crunching sound" when he breathed.
Antibiotics, painkillers and fluids cleared up the problem after 10 days.
Elborn's group tested the air pressure involved in blowing up balloons and found it was enough to damage the alveoli, the tiny sacs in the lung where air is absorbed.
A similar thing can happen when people "snort" cocaine or puff strongly at a marijuana joint, they said.
